children: Investors have long waited for PayPal's turnaround to gain some steam. A Wall Street firm, though, has begun to lose hope.
Cleveland Research downgraded shares of the payments company to Underperform from Neutral on Monday. Analyst Andrew Dusing wrote that he still sees PayPal's turnaround as "likely taking some time."

The turnaround, which began under CEO Enrique Lores when he joined in March, consists of a multiyear restructuring effort focused on cost-cutting and artificial-intelligence integration. Before that, in February, PayPal stock had lost nearly half its value over the preceding year after disappointing earnings and the announcement of the CEO transition.
Shares of PayPal declined 0.6% to $56.34 Monday. As of the close of trading Friday, the stock has fallen 2.9% this year.

Dusing wrote Monday that PayPal's branded checkout trends appeared weaker for the fiscal third quarter ended Sept. 30. Competitive pricing has also pressured Braintree, PayPal's unbranded payment processing service that merchants use behind the scenes to process credit card transactions. Rivals, like Adyen and Stripe, have offered discounted rates to lure merchants away, forcing Braintree to match low prices to retain clients, he wrote.

But even with discounted pricing, Braintree hasn't gained much market share, according to Cleveland Research. That's a difficult combination, leaving PayPal stuck sacrificing profit margins without getting growth in return. PayPal didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Monday's downgrade came after Bank of America cut PayPal's rating to Underperform from Neutral last week, saying the payments company faces a "long road ahead." The firm added that while the stock may look inexpensive, the analysts see "little to slow the erosion in the near term."

A lot has changed since PayPal released its second-quarter earnings on July 28. First, the company raised its 2026 outlook. But things took a turn the next month: The stock tumbled 13% on Aug. 28 following a report that Stripe and private-equity firm Advent International had walked away from acquisition negotiations, shifting investor attention away to PayPal's turnaround efforts.
Since the date of the company's latest earnings release, shares have gone up 4.9%. PayPal is set to report its third-quarter earnings on Oct. 27.
Of the 48 analysts covering the stock, 34 rate the stock as Hold while four recommend selling shares, according to FactSet.
